hints.title: Rotational Digit Pair Invariants
hints.text: Only a specific subset of digits look valid when rotated 180 degrees: zero, one, six, eight, and nine.

hints.title: Complementary Opposite Matching
hints.text: The character at the left index must match the rotated counterpart of the character at the mirrored right index.

hints.title: Inward Symmetrical Convergence
hints.text: Use two pointers converging inward. Map zero to zero, one to one, eight to eight, six to nine, and nine to six. If any character is not in the map or fails to equal its paired mirror, return false.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Constructing and reversing the entire inverted string uses unnecessary extra string allocations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two-pointer inward traversal validates pairs in-place with strictly O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize valid rotational pairs and properly handle middle character when N is odd.
